text.p: Following are some of the leading stories Norwegian papers this morning:

- Kolbjoern Almlid, head of the board of the organisation of power producers and distributors, says electricity prices will be high this winter because of low water levels in the country's hydropower reservoirs, but he rejects criticism from politicians that Norway's liberalised power market is not functioning.

- Between 1956 and 1963 750,000 Norwegians received a polio vaccine which was infected by a monkey virus. The virus has now been discovered to be carcinogenic. It is not known how many people have suffered from cancer as a result of the virus.
- Norwegian adventurer Boerge Ousland will try to cross the South Pole alone despite an unsuccessful attempt last year. The crossing is will start November 2 and is expected to last three months.

- Late on Monday night the boards of engineering and offshore group Aker ASA and investment group Resource Group International ASA (RGI) agreed to a merge of the two companies. The new concern will be called Aker RGI ASA. At the current share price Aker RGI will be one of the largest companies on the Oslo Bourse with a market capitalisation of nine billions crowns.
- Shares in drug company Nycomed ASA rose strongly on Tuesday on rumours it might be taken over. Nycomed A shares were up 6.45 percent and the B-shares were up 7.24 percent.
